correctness.rationale: For n>=5, the 2n edges of cyclic distances one and two are distinct. The vertex outdegree equation is equivalent in both directions to a_i+b_i=a_(i-1)+b_(i-2). Cyclic 8-state transitions encode all and only the balanced orientations with multiplicity one. The four closed state classes have weights 1,uv and 3x3 matrices with characteristic polynomials lambda(lambda^2-u lambda-v) and lambda(lambda^2-v lambda-u^2 v). Their n-th power traces give the stated binomial formula. The two families of exponent pairs and two extremes are disjoint for odd n. Program verify_direct.py exhaustively checks all 2^(2n) orientation assignments for n=5..9; verify_transfer.py checks the complete two-variable coefficient dictionaries for n=5..15. Neither finite check replaces the symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is the complete odd-order two-winding distribution, not the scalar count alone. A previous antiprism result concerns C_(2m)^2 and already provides the even-order unweighted count and a Lucas-cube structure; that case is excluded from novelty. Golin–Leung establish scalar recurrence machinery on circulants, while Felsner proves a planar orientation lattice and Isaev establishes high-connectivity asymptotics. None of the inspected full texts asserts the odd-order bivariate support or binomial multiplicities. Zhang–Shen (2007) is plausible prior scalar work but its full text was not available, leaving explicit priority risk; a title-only comparison is not evidence of noncoverage.

value.rationale: The odd squared-cycle family is a natural 4-regular circulant not represented by an integer-size antiprism. Its refined orientation partition function distinguishes two canonical jump directions; it is not merely an arbitrary finite slice or the previously known scalar Lucas count. The theorem shows the full bivariate support collapses from up to (n+1)^2 possible pairs to exactly n+3 specified pairs and supplies each coefficient, with two separate cyclic monomer-dimer sectors proved by the local-state dynamics. This exact windings law is useful for anisotropic orientation counts and for checking possible dynamics that preserve directed step counts. Neither a general recurrence-existence result nor an even-order orientation count implies the odd-order two-variable spectrum.
